critical.issue: 500 Internal Server Error — TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes. Line 1999: `if isinstance(upd, datetime) and upd >= cutoff:` — payment_transactions.updated_at is stored as naive datetime, but `cutoff` is tz-aware (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta). Impact: analytics endpoint fully broken for all window sizes (7/30/90). AnalyticsCard on /admin/products falls through to analytics-error state ('Sign in as admin to view analytics') even for authed users.

ui_bugs.issue: Error copy is misleading — reads 'Sign in as admin to view analytics' but real cause is backend 500. Should surface the actual error.detail (e.g., 'Failed to compute analytics') or a generic 'Try again later'.

integration_issues.issue: All three window switches (7/30/90) trigger backend 500 → analytics-stats never rendered on /admin/products. Blocked by admin_analytics tz bug above.

action_items: FIX BACKEND: /app/backend/server.py L1999 in admin_analytics — payment_transactions.updated_at is naive; make comparison timezone-safe. Suggested one-liner: `upd_tz = upd.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) if (isinstance(upd, datetime) and upd.tzinfo is None) else upd; if isinstance(upd_tz, datetime) and upd_tz >= cutoff:`. Alternatively, filter donations at the Mongo query with `{'updated_at': {'$gte': cutoff.replace(tzinfo=None)}}` (naive vs naive) or convert cutoff to naive for that specific filter.
Optional: surface actual backend error message in AnalyticsCard (err.response.data.detail) instead of the hard-coded admin-only string, so ops sees the real cause.

Optional: /community/starred should be re-fetched when the user context becomes available after login (in my test, D1 was seeded pre-starred but Community showed 'Star' initially — likely because the auth cookie/localStorage timing meant `user` context was null on first fetch).

rca of the issue: Line 1999 iterates payment_transactions and compares each doc's `updated_at` (which is a naive Python datetime object as read back from Mongo — pymongo returns BSON datetimes as tz-naive by default when not using tz_aware=True) against `cutoff` which is tz-aware (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta). Python raises TypeError when comparing naive and aware datetimes. Fix: normalize both to the same tz-awareness. Either construct `cutoff = datetime.utcnow() - timedelta(days=days)` (naive) for this loop, or apply `.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` to `upd` before comparing. The other cutoff-using queries in the same function that pass cutoff directly into Mongo (e.g. supporters aggregation) work fine because BSON date encoding strips tz info at the driver boundary; only the in-Python comparison breaks.
